messages:
maria: Heads up — I'm seeing steady KV-cache memory growth for tenant=acme on longctx workloads. Growth persists across >30m, paging activity spikes, and freeable pages aren't reclaimed. flamegraph: https://s3.redwood/insights/fg-acme-171800 · anyone seen this pattern before?

alex: Quick Q — is this the longctx path that pins KV pages (large attention caches)? any recent config changes to per-tenant quota or residency heuristics?

sandeep: I ran a quick mmap/pmap scan on the pod. lots of partially filled slabs and many pages with low "recent reuse" bits. evictions are happening but we aren't reclaiming because fragments are too small to coalesce. suspect fragmentation + reuse signature mismatch in the eviction-set logic.

perf-bot: perf-bot: benchmark kv-pagewalk-suite (2026-03-17T03:21Z) completed — median pagewalk time +12% vs baseline, tail 95% +28%. tagging @eng-runtime.

liz: Can you paste the small repro or a stack trace? Also, did we hit any per-tenant quota saturations?

maria: Repro is a longctx chat with many prompt edits (token churn). I captured a short trace and a heap map: https://s3.redwood/trace/acme-longctx-171800. no explicit quota errors in logs, usage looks stable.

alex: Two quick ideas: (1) add a per-tenant "recent_reuse_rate" counter so we can alert noisy tenants before they fragment slabs, (2) temporarily shorten the eviction window so pages become eligible faster. but watch for IO spikes.

sandeep: Agreed. Also noticed eviction classifier sometimes prefers old signatures over reuse probability when fragments are small. We should compute a reuse-signature fingerprint per-page and prefer eviction candidates with low fingerprint entropy.

maria: Short term plan: bump eviction window from 30s -> 10s for acme staging and run an aggressive slab sweep job. Long term: add reuse-signature fingerprint + per-tenant reuse_rate metric + reclaim-on-coalesce.

liz: I'll open a canary and add observability. sample adhoc commands I used to inspect residency:

```
# on pod
pmap -x $(pidof redwood-runtime) | grep kv_cache
cat /proc/vmstat | grep pgmajfault
# perf record -g -p <pid> -- sleep 30
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment created: canary/kv-evict-window-10s - id c-453. Staging rollout started.

alex: Important: watch batching heuristics and latency during canary. If eviction churn causes IO stalls, some requests might fall out of fast-paths and hit slower kernels. We'll need tracing on per-request latency and kernel selection counts.

maria: Copy. I'll attach perf+flamegraphs once the canary runs (perf record + flamegraph). Also collecting KV residency snapshots before/after.

sandeep: I'll add a quick dashboard panel: "tenant_reuse_rate" and "kv_fragmented_pages_percent" and set a temporary alert (warn if reuse_rate < 5% for 2m).

liz: :thumbsup: scheduling a post-mortem checkpoint after canary completes. tagging @eng-sre for rollout monitoring.

maria: Thanks all — will post traces and follow-ups here. If anyone wants to debug live, I can open the staging pod for pair debugging.
